label: Decode-first issue order
mechanism: the graphed decode step is handed to the GPUs BEFORE the step's prefill traversal and read back after it, so its ~163 ms of GPU work runs underneath prefill's ~1.2 s of pure host Python instead of queueing behind it
hypothesis: exp-0018/exp-0020 assumed the prefill traversal was GPU-bound and merely sync-pinned; this iteration measured that assumption and it is FALSE, which is why exp-0020 was rejected at 222.6 (null) and why the microbatched-prefill arm this iteration started with had to be abandoned. engine/pyengine/tests/t_traversal_sync_probe.py, real resident model, warm, every implicit device->host sync entry point counted by monkeypatch (log /workspace/logs/t_traversal_sync_probe_exp0021_out.log): (arm a) a grouped 3-row prefill traversal contains ZERO syncs — exp-0018 did exactly what it claimed; (arm b) that same traversal costs 696 ms of HOST time against a 0.1 ms DEVICE TAIL, repeated at 695/0.3 — the four GPUs finish everything the instant the host stops issuing; (arm c) two traversals back to back cost 1355 ms whether or not a full device sync separates them (1368/1355/1355/1355), i.e. there is no run-ahead to give away. Prefill is PYTHON-limited, not pipeline-limited. The microbatch arm confirms it from the other side (t_microbatch_prefill.py, interleaved arms, one load): cutting the 6-prompt cohort into 2 or 3 sub-group traversals cost 1.354 -> 1.544 -> 1.710 s on the mixed step, exactly one flat ~180 ms term per extra traversal with ZERO overlap realized; it ships OFF (_MICROBATCH=0, a no-op branch) with its evidence script so the negative result stays reproducible. ONE VARIABLE HERE: the order in which Scheduler.step hands its two independent traversals over. The graphed decode step is the opposite shape to prefill — a few ms of host work driving ~163 ms of GPU work — so it is enqueued FIRST (graphrun.step splits into step_enqueue/step_pick exactly as exp-0018 split prefill; Engine.decode_batch splits into decode_batch_enqueue/decode_batch_pick, and both original entry points survive as the enqueue+readback composition so every caller outside the scheduler is unchanged), and its single argmax readback is deferred behind the prefill Python. A mixed step then costs max(prefill host, decode GPU + prefill GPU) instead of the sum. The decode traversal is disjoint from this step's admissions by construction (admit_step == step_count, unchanged from exp-0018) and walks disjoint pool slots, so moving it earlier cannot read anything the prefills produce; the only other thing that moves is which page ids the shared free list hands out, which is storage, not arithmetic. NOTHING NUMERIC MOVES: identical kernels, identical shapes, identical per-row op order. MEASURED IN SITU (engine/pyengine/tests/t_decode_first.py, one resident load, GraphRunner warmed at the same key-length bucket so no capture lands in a timed arm, arms INTERLEAVED off/on/off/on; log /workspace/logs/t_decode_first_exp0021_out.log): the MIXED step — 6-prompt cohort landing on 8 already-decoding residents, the canonical steady state — goes 1.358 -> 1.234 s = 1.100x, -124 ms, i.e. 76% of the 163 ms decode step is hidden; repeats agree to 1 ms (1.362/1.354 off, 1.235/1.234 on). Prefill-only steps (1.534 -> 1.528) and decode-only steps (0.163 -> 0.163) do NOT move, as they must not. Kill switch PYENGINE_DECODE_FIRST=0 restores exp-0018's order. BASE, stated plainly: exp-0019 (e962f06, ACCEPTED, ledger iter 20, 222.9) merged with exp-0020 (ec60a25, REJECTED as null at 222.6 — rejected for thinness, not for being wrong, and its sync-free traversal is load-bearing for both the diagnosis above and the deferred prefill readback this mechanism composes with) and with current main; git merge-base --is-ancestor main e30e841 verified at spec time.
predicted_delta: +3.0 to +4.0% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 229-232 vs the best same-protocol accepted row 222.9 (merge bar 223.6). Cycle model, stated so it can be falsified: at cohort 6 the box's ~1083 requests release in ~180 cohorts, so ~180 of the ~2350 steps own both a prefill group and a decode traversal; 180 x 124 ms = 22.3 s off a ~620 s box = +3.7%. Unusually for this line of attack the count is ROBUST TO FRAGMENTATION in the helpful direction: if the bench's arrival pattern breaks cohorts into smaller admissions there are MORE mixed steps, and a singleton prefill (~380 ms of host time) still hides the whole 163 ms decode step, so the saving grows toward its 1083 x 124 ms = 134 s ceiling rather than evaporating the way exp-0014's and exp-0017's did. Floor case: if the server admits in far fewer steps than the cohort model predicts (long stretches of pure decode with rare, large admissions) the saving shrinks toward zero and the row lands at ~222.6-222.9 — a rejection that would still price the mixed-step share of the canonical box for the first time. prefill_heavy rides the same seam and should gain more (more admissions per box); remeasure later as a point row.
